Use twoPhaseEulerFoam to simulate steady-state two-phase oil-water flow in a horizontal pipe.
Set the pipe geometry to a diameter of 0.1 m and a length of 5 m.
Set the water density to 1000 kg/m3 and the water dynamic viscosity to 0.001 Pa·s.
Set the oil density to 850 kg/m3 and the oil dynamic viscosity to 0.01 Pa·s.
Impose a fixed mixture velocity of 1 m/s at the inlet.
Impose a fixed water volume fraction of 0.3 at the inlet.
Use noSlip boundary conditions on the pipe walls.
In 0/alpha.water, set the outlet boundary condition to zeroGradient, not fixedValue uniform 0.3.
Set the outlet velocity boundary condition to zeroGradient.
Set the outlet pressure boundary condition to fixedValue uniform 0.
Use the standard kEpsilon turbulence model for the simulation.
Run the simulation with twoPhaseEulerFoam until steady-state conditions are reached.
